text.description: Český Krumlov Castle is a huge castle complex that spreads along a steep, long rocky headland, with the Vltava running along its southern side. Its colourful tower and the layers of courtyards, bridges and walls make it easy to photograph from many angles, and because everything is stacked up the hillside, even a simple shot has plenty of depth. The first castle here dates back to 1253, built by the Vítkovci family, and the complex later passed through the Rosenbergs, the Eggenbergs and the Schwarzenbergs. It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1992 and is the second largest castle and chateau complex in the Czech Republic, after Prague Castle. Look out for the five-storey Cloak Bridge, dating from 1764, which joins the Upper Castle to the theatre building and gardens. The Baroque theatre from 1767 is counted among the best preserved in the world. Start with the whole castle and the tower, then move closer for details such as the bridges and the courtyard. Work at a relaxed pace: tap the screen on the part you want sharp, and check the edges of the frame for people and railings before you press the shutter.
text.geographic_location: In the town of Český Krumlov, on a steep, long rocky headland with the Vltava running along its southern side.
text.directions_text: The castle complex stands on the rocky headland. The phone icon on the map is about 30 m west of the subject. The Navigate buttons below take you straight there.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) for the castle and its setting. Switch to the ultra-wide (0.5x) if you are close and the walls and tower will not fit. Use the telephoto (2x-5x, depending on your phone) to pick out the tower, rooftops or the Cloak Bridge from a distance.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand about 30 m west of the subject, at the phone icon on the map, and face east. Face east, keep the phone level and let the castle fill the upper part of the frame.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on the gridlines and place the tower or the main mass of buildings on one of the vertical lines, with the rock and walls leading the eye up to it. Include a little foreground, such as a wall or the rooftops, to give a sense of scale. For close-up detail, use the telephoto instead of walking right up to the walls.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the castle walls to set focus, then slide the exposure control down slightly if the sky is bright, so the colours of the buildings stay rich. Take a few frames with the default lens (1x) and the ultra-wide (0.5x) so you can choose later.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Early morning or late afternoon usually gives softer light and fewer people in the shot. Midday can be harsh and bright, so check how the light looks on the walls before you shoot.

text.access_note: The castle complex includes ticketed areas as well as public parts, so check the official site before you go.

text.description: The Castle Gardens are part of the castle complex in Český Krumlov, and the best way to photograph them is from the bridge that leads in. From the garden end of Plášťový most (the Cloak Bridge), where the upper covered passage runs into the garden, you see the arcaded bridge framing the entrance. Beyond it are the castle buildings and the red roofs of the town. The arches give your photo a natural frame, and the roofs and towers behind them show where you are. Guides describe the Cloak Bridge as one of the most typical Krumlov views and a route into the garden. Walking across the outside of the bridge is free, but the bridge interior is only on the guided castle tour route. Opening hours for the garden vary by season, so check before you go. If you want the garden itself, step inside to Zámecká zahrada. There the stepped terrace and cascade fountain sit in the foreground, with the castle and garden walls behind. For a different angle, Seminární zahrada looks across the Vltava to the castle and its towers, with the terracotta roofs of the Old Town beside them. The garden is not clearly visible from there. Keep the bridge arches straight in your frame and let the roofs fill the background.
text.geographic_location: The Castle Gardens are on the castle side of Český Krumlov, beside the castle complex and reached over the Plášťový most (Cloak Bridge).
text.directions_text: Head for the Cloak Bridge, Plášťový most, and go to the garden end, where the upper covered passage leads into the garden. The phone icon on the map is about 330 m east of the subject. The Navigate buttons below take you straight there.

Use the telephoto (2x or more, depending on your phone) to pick out the roofs and castle details beyond the arches.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand about 330 m east of the subject, on Plášťový most (the phone icon on the map), and face west. Where the upper covered passage leads into the garden. From here your photo shows the arcaded bridge framing the entrance to the garden, with the castle buildings and the town's red roofs beyond.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on the gridlines and line up the bridge arches with the vertical lines so the arcade looks straight. Keep the castle buildings and red roofs in the upper part of the frame. For a close-up of the garden, go inside to Zámecká zahrada and shoot the terrace and cascade fountain with the castle behind. Seminární zahrada across the Vltava is an alternative for a view of the castle and towers with the Old Town roofs.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap the brightest part of the sky or the roofs to focus, then lower the exposure slider a little so the covered passage does not wash out the sky. If the arches are in shade, check that the roofs behind still look bright.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Visit when the garden is open, since hours vary by season.

text.access_note: Walking across the outside of the Cloak Bridge is free, but garden opening hours vary by season and the bridge interior is only on a guided castle tour, so check the official site before you go.

text.description:
The Minorite Monastery is a good example of Český Krumlov's layered skyline. From the phone icon on the map it is not a single building you frame on its own. Its garden and brewery rise among the houses to the right of the castle, so the monastery sits in the same picture as the castle complex, the river and the Old Town rooftops. That is why it works well on a phone: one frame tells the story of the town, with the monastery as a quieter detail beside the famous castle.

The viewpoint is Seminární zahrada, a park across the Vltava from the castle. It is a good place to see the monastery and castle together, with the river between you and them. Start with a wide view to take in the whole scene, then look to the right of the castle for the monastery garden and the roofs around it. A tighter second shot of that corner makes a nice contrast to the wide one.

Keep the horizon level, use the gridlines, and let the river or the rooftops fill the lower part of the frame so the picture has depth. If people walk through your view, wait a moment and take another. Whether you can go inside the monastery is a separate question, so check the official site before you go.
text.geographic_location: In Český Krumlov, in the park called Seminární zahrada on the opposite bank of the Vltava from the castle. The monastery itself lies among the houses to the right of the castle as you look across the river.
text.directions_text: Start from the Old Town of Český Krumlov and head for Seminární zahrada, the park across the Vltava from the castle. The phone icon on the map is about 290 m south-west of the subject. The Navigate buttons below take you straight there.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the ultra-wide (0.5x) for the full scene of castle, river and rooftops, then switch to the default lens (1x) for a cleaner view of the garden and brewery among the houses. Use telephoto (2x-5x, depending on your phone) to isolate the monastery to the right of the castle.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand about 290 m south-west of the subject, in Seminární zahrada (the phone icon on the map), and face north-east. Across the Vltava from the castle. Look north-east and you will see the monastery garden and brewery among the houses to the right of the castle, with the castle complex, the river and the Old Town rooftops in the same frame.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Put the castle on the left and the monastery garden and brewery on the right, with the river across the lower part of the frame. Turn on the gridlines to keep the horizon straight. Then take a tighter shot of just the monastery and its neighbouring roofs.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the monastery roofs to set focus, then drag the exposure slider down a little if the sky is bright so the buildings keep their colour. Try 2x or 3x for the close-up rather than pinching in further, which tends to look soft.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Early morning or late afternoon usually gives softer light and fewer people, but the view works at any time of day. Check the light on the day, as it changes with the season.

text.access_note: Seminární zahrada is a public park, but the monastery and its garden are not part of the viewpoint, so check the official site before you go if you want to visit inside.

text.description:
The Egon Schiele Art Centrum is a museum and gallery devoted to the Austrian painter Egon Schiele, and it sits in Český Krumlov (Krumau). It was set up in 1992 by a group of Czechs, Austrians and Americans. Since 1993 it has shown a permanent exhibition of Schiele's work, along with yearly displays of 20th-century art by names such as Picasso, Dalí and Klimt. That art connection gives you a different kind of picture from the usual town views: the street, the building and the people passing by.

Frame the museum building from the street as you approach it. Keep the frame simple: one clear building, a bit of street in front and some sky above.

Your phone handles this well. The default lens (1x) gives a natural view of the frontage. If the street is narrow and you cannot step back, switch to the ultra-wide (0.5x), but keep the building near the centre so the edges do not stretch. Turn on gridlines to keep the walls upright. Do not go inside to photograph the artworks without checking the rules first: check the official site before you go.

text.description:
This spot is where Linecká street meets the Vltava in Český Krumlov, and it is worth a few frames because you get a street, a river and the town's rooftops in one view. The river gives you a natural line to lead the eye through the picture, and the street adds the look of the old town. Together they make a scene that suits a phone photo.

The scene you want is about 63 metres away, so you can start with a wide view and then move closer for details. Begin with the ultra-wide lens (0.5x) if you want street, water and sky together, but keep any people or signs away from the edges, where ultra-wide lenses stretch things. The default lens (1x) gives a more natural look and is a good choice for most shots. If you want to pick out a single roofline or a reflection on the water, try the telephoto lens (2x or more, depending on your phone). Turn on the gridlines and line the river up with one of them so it does not tilt. Tap the brightest part of the picture to focus, then lower the exposure slider a little so the sky keeps its colour. Check the water's edge before you press the shutter, because railings and signs can creep into the frame. Stay aware of traffic and other walkers.
text.geographic_location: In Český Krumlov, on or near Linecká street by the Vltava.
text.directions_text: Make your way to the centre of Český Krumlov and head for the Vltava, then look for Linecká street beside the river. Use a map app to navigate to Linecká street. The phone icon on the map is about 15 m north-west of the subject. The Navigate buttons below take you straight there.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) for a natural view of street and river. Switch to ultra-wide (0.5x) to fit more in if the pavement is narrow, and use telephoto (2x or more, depending on your phone) for details such as rooftops or reflections.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand about 15 m north-west of the subject, at the phone icon on the map, and face south-east.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on the gridlines and place the river along one line so the horizon stays level. Use the street as a leading line towards the water, and keep the edges of the frame clear of bins, signs and passers-by.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the brightest area to focus, then drag the exposure slider down slightly so the sky and water keep their colour. Try a Live Photo to catch moving water or people walking past, and pick the best frame afterwards.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Early morning or early evening is usually calmer and has softer light. At dusk, use night mode and rest your elbows on something firm to keep the phone steady.

text.access_note: This looks like an ordinary street by the river and should be open to walk along, but check the official site before you go if you plan to enter any nearby attraction.

name: Barber's Bridge (Lazebnický most)
label: Barber's Bridge
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Latrán' (2 web pages); placed at OpenStreetMap 'Latrán' (node/1599136525): point.
pin_note: Position from OpenStreetMap way/759607097: kept: no OpenStreetMap object carries this Wikidata ID.

text.description:
Barber's Bridge (Lazebnický most) crosses the river in the old part of Český Krumlov. The classic views are looking out from the bridge, but this spot is about photographing the bridge itself. The best way to do that is from Latrán, the street guides describe as the main walking route to the bridge. As you walk down towards the river, the bridge closes the far end of the street, with the castle rising beyond it. That layering of street, bridge and castle is what makes the picture work on a phone. The street leads the eye straight to the bridge, and the castle gives the frame a clear background.

Stand on Latrán at the Spičák end, at the phone icon on the map, and look south-west along the street. The bridge is a short walk ahead of you. Keep the bridge in the centre and let the street edges frame it. If you want a second picture, walk onto the bridge for the view of the castle and river. The bridge isn't in that frame, so it only works if you want it as a foreground element.

The bridge has been closed for reconstruction in the past, so check it is open before you plan your walk. Whatever you find, the street view of the bridge from Latrán is worth taking.
text.geographic_location: In the old town of Český Krumlov, where the street Latrán runs down towards the river and ends at the bridge. The castle rises behind the bridge when seen from the Spičák end of the street.
text.directions_text: Walk into the old town of Český Krumlov and down Latrán towards the river. The phone icon on the map is about 150 m north-east of the subject. The Navigate buttons below take you straight there.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) so the bridge, the street edges and the castle all fit in one frame. If the street is crowded or you can't step back, the ultra-wide (0.5x) fits more in. Use the telephoto (2x-5x, depending on your phone) to bring the castle and bridge closer together.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand about 150 m north-east of the subject, on Latrán (the phone icon on the map), and face south-west. On Latrán, at the Spičák end, where the bridge closes the street. From here you see the bridge with the castle rising beyond it.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Switch on gridlines and put the bridge on the centre line, with the street's building edges on both sides as a frame. Keep the camera level so the street doesn't lean. For a second shot, walk onto the bridge to photograph the castle and river, though the bridge itself won't be in that frame.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the bridge to set focus, then drag the exposure slider down slightly so the sky and castle keep their detail. Take a few frames while people walk through, and keep the one with the clearest view of the bridge.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Early morning or later in the evening is likely to leave fewer people in the street, so the bridge is easier to frame cleanly.

text.access_note: Latrán is a public street, but the bridge has been closed for reconstruction in the past, so check it is open before you go.
claims_not_in_sources: Early morning or later in the evening is usually quieter on the street, giving a cleaner view of the bridge.
Telephoto zoom makes the castle look closer to the bridge in the frame.
Dragging the exposure slider down helps keep detail in a bright sky.

name: Rafting on the Vltava weir
label: Vltava weir
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Jelení lávka' (3 web pages); placed at OpenStreetMap 'Jelení lávka' (way/760743635): middle (52 m across).
pin_note: Position from OpenStreetMap way/586690430: kept: no OpenStreetMap object carries this Wikidata ID.

text.description:
This is the weir on the Vltava just below Český Krumlov castle, known as Jez U Jelení lávky. Its wide sluice is where rafts and canoes run down the river, and rafts shooting the wide passage of the weir make a good spectacle, which is what makes the spot worth a photo. Visitors often stop to watch it, and the rafts passing through make a lively scene.

The best view is from Jelení lávka, the footbridge over the weir. From there you are above the water and close to it, so the rafts, paddles and spray all fit into one frame. The left bank of the weir is the other place where people gather to watch.

Rafting trips on the river generally run from May to September, so outside that season the water may be empty of boats. If you arrive and nothing is happening, wait a few minutes.

For your phone, keep your arms steady on the bridge rail and decide beforehand where in the frame the raft will appear. Tap the water just where the raft will come through so the focus is ready before it arrives. Keep other people's heads out of the foreground, and take a few shots as each raft passes rather than relying on one.
text.geographic_location: The weir is on the Vltava below the castle in Český Krumlov, and the Jelení lávka footbridge crosses it.
text.directions_text: No station or tram stop is listed for this spot. From the phone icon on the map, walk south towards the river below the castle and look for the footbridge over the weir. The phone icon on the map is about 640 m north of the subject. The Navigate buttons below take you straight there.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) on the footbridge so you get the weir, the river and the raft together. Switch to telephoto (2x-5x, depending on your phone) to pick out one raft and its paddlers as it comes through the sluice. The ultra-wide (0.5x) works if you want the whole weir and the castle above it, but boats will look small.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand about 640 m north of the subject, on Jelení lávka (the phone icon on the map), and face south. The place to shoot from is Jelení lávka, the footbridge over the weir below the castle. From the bridge you look down on the wide sluice, where the rafts and canoes run through close to the water. The left bank of the weir is a second place to watch from.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on gridlines and place the sluice on one of the lower lines, leaving room above for the raft to drop into the frame. Shoot along the flow of the water so the raft heads towards you or across the frame, not away. Keep the bridge rail out of the picture, or use it only as a soft foreground edge.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap the water at the point where the raft will pass to lock focus, then slide the exposure down a little so the white water doesn't turn pale. Turn on Live Photos or motion so you can pick the best frame afterwards. Wipe the lens first, as spray can leave marks.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Choose a daytime visit between May and September, when rafting trips generally run.

text.access_note: The footbridge is a public crossing with no charge noted.
